name: SKAdNetwork 4 (postbacks)
plain: Apple sends the ad network a signed, delayed, anonymized report that an ad led to an install.
meaning: Gives ad networks proof an ad drove an install without a device ID. Reports are coarse, delayed and may be dropped for small campaigns.

ios.permission: SKAdNetworkItems (Info.plist, network IDs); app calls SKAdNetwork.updatePostbackConversionValue
ios.persistence: Apple signs postbacks; app and ad network never see device IDs
ios.store_policy: App Review: no fingerprinting; ATT not required for SKAN
ios.note: SKAN 4 (iOS 16.1): three postbacks, hierarchical source ID (2 to 4 digits), coarse and fine values, web-to-app.

data.update: up to 3 postbacks per install, each delayed

limits.headline: Can tell an ad network an ad led to an install, in a delayed report
limits.user_action: You tap an ad, install the app, then use it for a few days
can: Send a signed report that an ad led to an install
Send up to three reports over weeks
Show a small campaign number (2 to 4 digits)
cannot: Give your name or device ID
Report the same day; delays and low counts remove detail
Work on Android; it uses the install referrer
limits.differs: iPhone only (iOS 11.3 and later; iOS 16.1 for the newest version). Android uses the install referrer.

story.what_it_is: Apple's system that tells an ad network an ad led to an install, in a delayed, anonymous report.

marketing.name: SKAdNetwork
marketing.pitch: A privacy preserving way to measure ad driven installs without revealing user or device level data.

story.for_you: You tap an ad, install and open the app. Days later Apple sends the ad network a signed note that one install came from that ad, with no name or device ID.
story.for_makers: It gives ad networks proof an ad drove an install, without an ID. Reports are coarse and delayed and may be dropped for small campaigns, so makers choose their budgets with less detail than before.

use_cases.example: A game studio finds out a video ad brought 500 installs and ties them to a coarse revenue band.
A retail app confirms an ad brought installs, but cannot see which person.
An ad network gets signed proof so it can bill the advertiser without a device ID.
A social app learns which campaign brought sign ups after seven days.
A marketing team compares SKAN data with its own sales data to see the gap.
Signatures stop fake networks from claiming installs they did not drive.

story.android_note: Android has no SKAN. Google used the install referrer and advertising ID.
story.ios_note: SKAdNetwork 4 added three postback windows and coarse values.

technical_bounds: Postbacks to the ad network only (app developer does not get it directly)
Crowd anonymity tiers cut data on small campaigns

abuse: Abused by conversion-value encoding to infer behavior

history.change: Version 3 plus ATT, becomes the default measure for non-consented users
SKAN 4: multiple postbacks, hierarchical IDs, coarse values, web-to-app
AdAttributionKit introduced as the successor framework
